heroText: Fes is Morocco's spiritual and intellectual capital, home to Fes el-Bali, the world's largest car-free urban medina and a UNESCO World Heritage site. First-time visitors should enter through Bab Boujloud, watch hides being dyed at the Chouara Tannery, and admire the carved cedar of the Bou Inania Madrasa. Fes-Saiss Airport sits a short drive away, and the Fes Festival of World Sacred Music draws visitors each spring.

areas.name: Fes el-Bali
areas.text: Fes el-Bali is the ancient walled medina, a UNESCO-listed maze of souks, mosques and workshops best explored on foot or with a guide.

areas.name: Fes el-Jdid
areas.text: Fes el-Jdid is the 13th-century royal quarter next to the old medina, home to the Royal Palace gates and the historic Jewish Mellah.

areas.name: Ville Nouvelle
areas.text: Ville Nouvelle is the French-built new town, with modern hotels, restaurants and wider streets away from the medina's crowds.

areas.name: Batha
areas.text: Batha sits at the medina's edge near the Dar Batha museum and Jnan Sbil Gardens, a convenient base close to both old and new town.

airports.name: Fes-Saiss Airport (FEZ)
airports.text: Fes-Saiss Airport lies about 15 kilometres south of the city; taxis and hotel transfers cover the short ride into the medina or Ville Nouvelle.

airportTransfer.value: Compare road transfer time between Fes-Saiss Airport (FEZ) and central Fes before choosing an airport-area or city-centre hotel.

stayOverview: Stay inside Fes el-Bali in a converted riad for the most atmospheric first visit, close to Bab Boujloud and the Chouara Tannery, or choose Ville Nouvelle for modern hotels and easier road access. Batha offers a useful middle ground near the gardens and museums.
hotelIntro: Riads inside Fes el-Bali offer the most memorable stays, steps from the tannery and madrasas, while Ville Nouvelle's hotels suit travelers wanting modern comforts, parking and a wider dining scene beyond the medina walls.
rentalCars: A rental car is unnecessary and impractical inside the medina's narrow lanes, though useful for day trips into the Middle Atlas once parked outside the old city.

travelTips.title: Hire a medina guide
travelTips.text: Fes el-Bali's medina has thousands of winding lanes, so a licensed guide saves time and helps avoid unofficial 'guides' near the gates.

travelTips.title: Visit the tannery mid-morning
travelTips.text: See the Chouara Tannery from a surrounding leather shop's terrace mid-morning, when the dye pits are most active and the light is best.

travelTips.title: Book a riad early
travelTips.text: Reserve a riad inside the medina well ahead during the Fes Festival of World Sacred Music, when accommodation fills quickly.

travelTips.title: Comfortable shoes matter
travelTips.text: Keep the Fes plan compact: group nearby sights together and leave enough time for transfers, meals and weather changes.

history.text: The two cities were united in 1070 and the name Fās was used for the combined site.
Towards the end of World War II, Moroccan nationalists gathered in Fez to draft a demand for independence which they submitted to the Allies on 11 January 1944.
In 1963 the University of Al-Qarawiyyin was reorganized as a state university, while a new public university, Sidi Mohamed Ben Abdellah University, was founded in 1975 in the Ville Nouvelle.
